hints: Look at the overall shape in the x60 photomicrograph. Notice the thick circular wall and the relatively small, round central lumen. Which mammalian blood vessel has this appearance?
Remember the three wall layers of that vessel from lumen outwards. Which middle layer is thick and dark-staining here, and what two tissues let it stretch and constrict?
walkthrough:
**Identify the structure**

First, look at the big picture. You see a circular tube in transverse section with a very thick wall and a clear central lumen.

That thick wall with a small lumen is classic for an artery, not a vein or capillary.

**Recall the artery wall layers**

An artery has three layers from inside to outside. The tunica intima is the thin endothelium lining the lumen. The tunica media is the thick middle layer. The tunica externa is the outer connective tissue layer.

**Locate layer W and name its contents**

The label line for W points to the thick, dark-staining middle band of the wall. That is the tunica media.

The tunica media of an artery is made mainly of smooth muscle to allow vasoconstriction, plus elastic fibres to allow stretch and recoil with each pulse. That matches option C.

options.A: Collagen fibres only describes the tough outer tunica externa, not the thick muscular middle layer W.
options.B: Elastic fibres plus collagen fibres without muscle is more like the outer layer, W contains abundant smooth muscle as well.
options.C: W is the tunica media of the artery, whose main components are smooth muscle and elastic fibres for constriction, stretch and recoil.
options.D: Squamous epithelial cells forming an endothelium is the very thin tunica intima lining the lumen, not the thick layer W.
